sections.label: Higher tax rates for top incomes
sections.summary: Chargeable income above $500,000 up to $1 million will be taxed at 23%, and above $1 million at 24%, up from 22%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The portion of chargeable income in excess of $500,000 up to $1 million will be taxed at 23%, while that in excess of $1 million will be taxed at 24% – both up from 22% today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This move would further enhance the progressivity of our PIT system, where individuals who earn more will contribute more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We estimate that this could raise around $170 million of additional tax revenue per year.

sections.label: IRAS disclosing company information
sections.summary: The amendment lets IRAS disclose a prescribed list of identifiable company-related information to other public sector agencies without taxpayer consent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: To enable public sector agencies to carry out their official duties more effectively, the proposed amendment enables IRAS to disclose a prescribed list of identifiable company-related information to other public sector agencies, for the performance of official duties, without requiring the taxpayer’s consent.

sections.label: Board of Review provisions amended
sections.summary: BOR provisions will be updated and streamlined, including removing outdated references, clarifying regulation-making and case management powers, and allowing a one-member coram.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Second, we will amend the provisions relating to the Board of Review, also known as the BOR, which is a tribunal set up under the Income Tax Act to hear and adjudicate tax disputes between the Comptroller and taxpayers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The BOR provisions will be updated and streamlined by: (a) removing outdated references such as the requirement for lodgement of the notice of appeal in “duplicate” and the petition of appeal in "quadruplicate", which are no longer relevant where documents are sent digitally, (b)	clarifying the Minister's regulation-making powers regarding tax appeals, as well as the case management powers of the BOR and chairperson, and (c)	moving BOR provisions on procedures to subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In addition, we propose to allow the chairperson to have the option to convene a one-member coram where appropriate.

sections.label: IRAS information disclosure to agencies
sections.summary: One change lets IRAS disclose information to other Government agencies with taxpayer consent, and another allows company-related information disclosure without consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The first change grants powers to IRAS to disclose information to other Government agencies for the purpose of performing official duties as long as the taxpayers have given consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The second change allows IRAS to disclose to other Government agencies company-related information without the consent of taxpayer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Both changes are intended to support data-driven policy setting, improved public office operations and integrated service delivery.

sections.label: Headline inflation at 14-year high
sections.summary: Headline inflation reached 7.5%, a 14-year high last seen during the Global Financial Crisis in mid-2008.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Headline inflation clocked in at a scorching 7.5%, a 14-year high last experienced during the throes of the Global Financial Crisis in mid-2008.

sections.label: Core inflation at 5.1%
sections.summary: Core inflation, which strips out private transportation and accommodation, struck 5.1%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What is worse, core inflation, the stable component of price increases, which strips out the more volatile components of private transportation and accommodation struck 5.1%.

sections.label: Tax revenue surge reported
sections.summary: IRAS reported tax revenue rose more than 22% for financial year 2021/2022 after the speech.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the time that the speech was delivered, IRAS subsequently reported that tax revenue surged by more than 22% for the financial year 2021/2022.

sections.label: Fiscal surplus rebate objection
sections.summary: An objection that higher revenue reflects a low base is countered by $60.7 billion being above the prior three-year average.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One immediate objection to rebating fiscal surpluses is that the increase is only reflective of a low base from repressed collections in the prior year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But the revenues of $60.7 billion booked last year is not only larger than the low base of $49.6 billion booked last fiscal year, understandably due to pandemic related reasons, but also almost $9 billion higher than the average of the three years before.

sections.label: Lawrence Wong support package
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a $1.5 billion support package in June, leaving $7.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In June, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a $1.5 billion support package, which still leaves $7.2 billion on the table.

sections.label: Inflation eroding voucher claim
sections.summary: Inflation eroded the claim, with vouchers covering less than 19 years for HDB 1- and 2-bedroom flats.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The reality of this claim has now since been eroded by inflation and the vouchers would only make up less than 19 years for those in HDB 1- and 2-bedroom flats, and between one and six months less for others.

sections.label: Workers' Party GST hike opposition
sections.summary: The Workers' Party remains opposed to the GST hike, citing alternative revenue sources, but urges softening the blow if it proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The point is that exercising, any one of these options or them in combination, can make a significant difference to the immediate financial circumstances faced by our struggling households.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party remains opposed to a GST hike for reasons that we have previously articulated – not least because we believe that there are alternative revenue sources that could still be tapped.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, if the GST hike must go ahead now, the least we can do is to further soften the blow with tools that we already have in hand.

sections.label: Penalties under Income Tax Act and PDPA
sections.summary: Section 94 of the Income Tax Act and the PDPA set out penalties for offences including unauthorised disclosure of personal data.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would that be under section 94 of the Income Tax Act, which states that the penalty is a maximum $5,000 fine and in default, imprisonment not exceeding six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the PDPA, the penalty for unauthorised disclosure of personal data is a maximum $5,000 fine or imprisonment, not exceeding two years or both.

sections.label: Parliament debate on decisions
sections.summary: Any such decision should be justified and debated in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Any such decision should be justified and debated in Parliament.

sections.label: IRAS information sharing provisions
sections.summary: The Bill includes provisions to allow IRAS to share information to public officers and other authorised people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill includes provisions to allow IRAS to share information to public officers and other authorised people.

sections.label: IRAS disclosure without consent
sections.summary: The new section 6(12B) allows IRAS to disclose certain prescribed information without consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fourth, the new section 6(12B) allows IRAS to disclose certain prescribed information without consent.

sections.label: Single member BOR hearings
sections.summary: The new section 78 allows the BOR chairperson to appoint a single member to hear a case if issues are not complex.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the new section 78 will allow the chairperson of the Board of Review (BOR) to appoint a single member of the Board to hear a case if the issues involved are not complex.

sections.label: Top personal income tax rates
sections.summary: From Year of Assessment 2024, chargeable income above $500,000 up to $1 million is taxed at 23% and above $1 million at 24%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The headline change in this amendment Bill is the announced increase in the top marginal personal income tax rate with effect from Year of Assessment 2024, where chargeable income in excess of $500,000 up to $1 million will be taxed at 23% instead of 22%, while chargeable income in excess of $1 million will be taxed at 24% instead of 22%.

sections.label: Assumptions for additional tax revenue
sections.summary: The passage asks what main assumptions underlie the projected $170 million in additional tax revenue per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Further, what are the main assumptions underlying the projected $170 million in additional tax revenue per year?

sections.label: IRAS Rental Support Scheme payouts
sections.summary: IRAS data across tax types was used to automatically disburse over 110,000 payouts worth almost $1 billion under the Rental Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As Minister Indranee had shared during this year's Committee of Supply debate, IRAS' data across various tax types was used to automatically disburse more than 110,000 payouts worth almost $1 billion under the Rental Support Scheme.

sections.label: Single member hearing appeals
sections.summary: The amendments let the Board chairperson appoint a single member, instead of a three-member committee, to hear appeals in a particular case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under the amendments, the chairperson of the Board may appoint a single member, instead of a committee of three members, to hear appeals in a particular case.

sections.label: Authorised officers appearing before Board
sections.summary: The proposed new section 80(2) will not prevent a duly authorised officer of an appellant company, including in-house counsel, from appearing at the Board hearing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can I also clarify that the proposed new section 80(2) will not prevent a duly authorised officer of an appellant company, including in-house counsel, from appearing at the hearing before the Board?

sections.label: Moving away from preceding-year basis
sections.summary: The passage asks what hurdles prevent moving from a preceding-year basis to one matching tax payments with contemporaneous income for better cash flow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What are the hurdles that would prevent us from moving away from a preceding-year basis to one that can allow Singaporeans to better manage their cash flow by matching tax payments with contemporaneous income?

sections.label: Increase in PIT rates
sections.summary: The PIT rate increase affects the top 1.2% of PIT taxpayers, about 35% of PIT revenue, raising around $170 million yearly based on YA2020 taxpayer base.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The increase in PIT rates will affect the top 1.2% of PIT taxpayers, who account for about 35% of our total PIT revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We estimate that this change would raise around $170 million of additional tax revenue per year based on the actual taxpayer base in Singapore in the Year of Assessment 2020 (YA2020).

sections.label: IRAS surcharge for tax avoidance
sections.summary: In tax avoidance cases, IRAS has powers under the Income Tax Act to impose a 50% surcharge on the amount of tax imposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In cases of tax avoidance, IRAS also has powers under the Income Tax Act to impose a surcharge of 50% on the amount of tax imposed by IRAS.

sections.label: Chairperson discretion not hardwired
sections.summary: The factors guiding the chairperson's discretion will not be hardwired in regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In relation to Mr Saktiandi Supaat's query, we will not hardwire the factors guiding the exercise of the chairperson's discretion in regulations.

sections.label: Objections lead to rehearing
sections.summary: If any party objects, the matter will be reheard by a new hearing committee or newly appointed single-member committee to ensure fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If any party objects, the matter will have to be reheard either by a new hearing committee or the newly appointed single-member committee to ensure fairness to the parties.

sections.label: IRAS disclosure for official duties
sections.summary: The proposed amendment to section 6(12) allows IRAS to disclose information for purposes beyond administering a written law or public scheme, if for official duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The proposed amendment to section 6(12) in this Bill allows IRAS to disclose such information for purposes beyond that of administering a written law or public scheme as long as it is for official duties.

sections.label: Prescribed company-related information list
sections.summary: The prescribed list under section 6(12B) is limited to company-related information frequently required by public sector agencies, including revenue range and tax deduction indications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The prescribed list of information under section 6(12B) is limited to company-related information that have been more frequently required by public sector agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This includes the range of revenue earned by the company and a yes-or-no indication on whether the company has claimed tax deductions such as for R&D expenditure in Singapore or expenditure on overseas business development.

sections.label: Penalties for unlawful disclosure
sections.summary: Unlawful disclosure under section 6 of the Income Tax Act carries penalties under section 94, with a maximum fine of $5,000 or imprisonment not exceeding six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For unlawful disclosure constituting an offence under section 6 of the Income Tax Act, penalties under section 94 would apply and this carries a maximum fine of $5,000 or in default of which imprisonment not exceeding six months.
